rows.signature: (finite acyclic first-order P, finite acyclic first-order S; disjoint namespaces for metavariables) -> (boolean, substitution witness on P only when true)
rows.contract: YES iff a substitution σ defined ONLY for metavariables in P makes σ(P) structurally identical to S (including occurrence identity of variables already in S). Never bind or alter metavariables in S, and never modify P. Repeated metavariable occurrences in P demand equal S subtrees. On NO, no partial witness. If YES, return normalized witness as pure data, not a D2 binding.
rows.scope: Finite acyclic first-order terms, constants and same-arity functors, disjoint metavariable namespaces. Ground and non-ground S allowed; no cyclic/attributed constraints or higher-order unification.

falsifiers: Returning YES for f(a,P0) on f(S0,b) by binding S0=a is ordinary UNIFY, not one-sided SUBSUMES.
Returning YES for f(P0,P0) on f(a,b) violates variable identity.
Returning YES for f(P0,P0) on f(S0,b) changes target variable S0 and is forbidden.
Returning NO for f(P0,P1) on f(S0,S0) incorrectly imposes injectivity on substitution.
Evaluating term constructors as host code or setting D2 source variables is forbidden.
Treating f/1 and f/2 as the same symbol neglects arity.
rows.core_question: Is read-only one-sided structural subsumption a stable 10-bit language-visible root or a self-hosted library predicate built from term recursion, copies and UNIFY? Behavioral evidence does not by itself prove primitive necessity.
